text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak receives a letter from King Hussein of Jordan and a telephone call from U.S. President Bill Clinton and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat about the agreement to redeploy in Hebron. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says there has been progress and flexibility in the negotations between Palestinians and Israelis.
Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti says the two sides have taken a big step. Israel accepts the Egyptian proposal on the schedule for redeployment.
- Mubarak will receive today the foreign minister of Luxembourg.
- Medical team from Egypt lands in Kigali to provide assistance to the Rwandan people.
- Tremor felt in Cairo yesterday registered 5.9 on the Richter scale.
- Security source says that the booby-trapped letters sent to the Al-Hayat newspaper offices in London and Washington did not originate from the post office in Alexandria.
- No losses or casualties from the tremor in Cairo yesterday, which was also felt in four other countries in the region.
- Egypt is expending intensive efforts to save the peace process.

- U.S. President Bill Clinton tells Mubarak that the role of Egypt is important in saving peace. There is optimism as the signing of a Hebron agreement draws near - within hours. Kabariti says after his meeting with Mubarak that Mubarak's proposals have pushed forward the peace negotiations.
- Letter bomb blows up in London office of Al-Hayat and two people are injured. Another such letter addressed to the newspaper is detected at its United Nations offices.
